deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a German prose notebook on Greek history, specifically the late phase of the Peloponnesian War (c. 411–406 BC). It reads like lecture or reading notes and continues seamlessly from the previous page (92) into the next (94). Its content is as follows.

(1) Alcibiades, now with the Persian satrap Tissaphernes, sends envoys to the Athenian army and fleet stationed on Samos. He promises them a powerful ally (Persia) if Athens makes its constitution aristocratic.

(2) In consequence, the Athenian assembly is restricted to 5000 citizens. Alcibiades is formally recalled and leads the Athenians from 411 to 407.

(3) Sparta turns to the satrap Pharnabazus, who strengthens its fleet and supplies auxiliary troops. The war shifts to the 'coasts of Thrace' (Hellespont/Propontis).

(4) Alcibiades wins several victories, said to be three at sea and one on land. At Cyzicus he defeats the land army and the fleet on the same day, securing Athenian control of the sea.

(5) In 407 he returns to Athens with richly laden fleets. After minor failures he is banished and lives in a castle on the Thracian coast.

(6) In 407 Cyrus the Younger arrives as satrap and is won over by Sparta, which now has Lysander as commander. Lysander is described as 'of the greatest talents but without all morality'. He wins a naval victory (dated 407 in the note) and is succeeded in 406 by Callicratidas.

There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct. The bundle label 'HB.Lagrange1816' notwithstanding, this folio is historical notes. The hand and content suggest school or lecture notes, possibly not by Gauss himself.
errors: The battle of Cyzicus took place in 410 BC. The note's framing ('von 411 — 407') is loose but does not misdate it explicitly.
Alcibiades was recalled by the fleet at Samos in 411. His formal recall and return to Athens came in 407. The note compresses these into a single formal recall by the 5000.
Lysander's naval victory at Notium is usually dated 406 BC (some chronologies say late 407). Alcibiades' second exile followed Notium, so 406 is more usual than the note's sequence implies.
Cyzicus lies on the Propontis in Mysia (Asia Minor), not in Thrace. 'Coasts of Thrace' is only loosely right for the Hellespont/Propontis theatre.
Context from page 92: the Spartan fortification of Decelea is usually dated 413 BC, not 414.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is non-mathematical historical notes summarizing a standard textbook account of the Peloponnesian War. There is no mathematical content, and nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematical work.

checkable.asserts: The span of Alcibiades' leadership as given in the note (411–407 BC) is 4 years. This is trivial date arithmetic; the page has no mathematical content.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'postirt[?]' is plausibly 'postirt' (= postiert). The reading is uncertain but fits the context.
Line 10: 'an der Spitze der[?]' is uncertain; the word may be 'bis' or a scribal abbreviation before 'von 411 — 407'.
The marginal note 'F der Athener' on the right is an insertion keyed to 'Herrschaft ... zur See'. It belongs after 'Herrschaft', reading 'Herrschaft der Athener zur See'.
Line 3 opening: the verb before 'jetzt Gesandte' is hard to read; 'schickte' is a contextual guess.
